greek: ἃ καὶ τὰς μικρὰς ἰᾶται φλεγμονάς τῶν συνθέτων μαλακτικῶν τὰ μέν ἐστιν ὡς ἂν εἴποι τις ἀσθενέστερα κατὰ τὴν πρώτην τάξιν ἔνια δὲ οὐ πολλῷ τούτων ἰσχυρότερα κατὰ δευτέραν καί τινα κατὰ γ΄ ἕτερα καὶ πρὸς αὐτοῖς κατὰ δ΄ ἄλλα χρῆσθαι δὲ προσῆκεν ὡς προείρηται πρὸς μὲν τὰς βραχείας σκληρότητας καὶ τὰ μαλακὰ σώματα τοῖς τῆς πρώτης τάξεως πρὸς δὲ τὰ τούτων ἰσχυρότερα σώματά τε καὶ πάθη τοῖς τῆς δευτέρας ὥσπερ γε καὶ τοῖς τῆς τρίτης καὶ τῆς τετάρτης ἀνάλογον ὑπογράφουσι δὲ καὶ τὰ καθ’ ἑκάστην αὐτῶν ἰδίᾳ Μαλακτικὰ φάρμακα πρώτης τάξεως Βούτυρον ἢ ῥητίνη ἡ Κολοφωνία καὶ κηρὸς λευκὸς μὴ παλαιὸς ἴσα τῷ σταθμῷ τὰ γ΄ τηκόμενα μετ’ ἀλλήλων μαλακτικὰ πρώτης τάξεώς ἐστι καὶ ἡ πάρυγρος ὅταν ᾖ πρόσφατος
translation_A: which also heal small inflammations. Of the compound emollients some are, as one might say, weaker, in the first rank; some not much stronger than these, in the second; and some others in the third, and besides these others in the fourth. One should use them, as was said before, for slight indurations and soft bodies, those of the first rank; for those stronger than these, both bodies and affections, those of the second; just as also those of the third and of the fourth proportionally. They write out also those of each of them separately. Emollient drugs of the first rank: Butter or Colophonian resin and white wax, not old, equal in weight, the 3 melted together, are emollients of the first rank; also the parygros when it is fresh
translation_B: which also heal the small inflammations. Of the compound emollients, some are, as one might say, weaker, in the first order; some not much stronger than these, in the second; and some in the third, and others besides these in the fourth. One should use, as was said before, for slight hardnesses and soft bodies those of the first order; for those stronger than these, both bodies and affections, those of the second, just as also those of the third and of the fourth proportionally. They also describe those in each of them separately. Emollient drugs of the first order: butter, or Colophonian resin of the pine, and white wax not old, equal in weight, the 3 melted together, are emollient of the first order; and so is the parygros, when it is fresh.

greek: Ἰοῦ δὲ χαλκοῦ καὶ ἀλόης Ἰνδικῆς Χαλκοῦ τε κεκαυμένου καὶ διφρυγοῦς καλοῦ Ἑκκαίδεχ ἥμισυ ἐξ ἑκάστου μίγματος Εἴκοσι δραχμὰς δὲ χαλβάνης καὶ δ΄ Μάννης λιβάνου τε τὰς ἴσας δὶς ιβ΄ Ἀμμωνιακοῦ δὶς ε΄ καὶ δὶς κ΄ Ἑκκαίδεκα δραχμὰς προπόλεως τῆς Ἀττικῆς Ἀριστολοχίας τῆς μακρᾶς δὶς ι΄ δραχμὰς Δὶς στ΄ λεπίδος τοῦ Κυπρίου χαλκοῦ δραχμὰς Καὶ γεντιανῆς ξηροτάτης ῥίζης ἴσον Τούτοις προσαπόδος πᾶσι δικτάμνου πόας Ξηρᾶς ἐχούσης ἄνθος ὁλκὰς κ΄ Λείας λιθάργυρον δὲ μετ’ ἐλαίου βαλὼν Εἰς λοπάδα καινὴν κεραμίαν πλατύστομον Ἕψε πυρὶ κούφῳ καὶ μαλακῷ κινῶν σπάθῃ Ἕως γένηται μέλιτος Ἀττικοῦ πάχος Ἴσον δὲ καὶ τῆς λεπίδος προσβαλὼν πάλιν Ἕψε λαβρότερον εἶτα κιῤῥοῦ γενομένου Τοῦ φαρμάκου πρόσβαλε χαλκὸν καὶ διφρυγὲς Ποιῶν τ’ ἀμόλυντον καὶ πεπηγὸς φάρμακον Πρόσβαλλε κηρὸν τήν τε

greek: Πάντων ἐπιμελῶς πάλιν ἀπόσταξον βραχύ μὲν βλέπῃς εὔχρουν τε καὶ κεκραμένην Ἄρον παραχρῆμα τὴν χύτραν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς Καὶ χαλβάνην πρόσβαλλε προμεμαλαγμένην Ἂν δ’ ᾖ παρὰ πολὺ σκληρότερον τὸ φάρμακον Ἔλαιον αὐτῷ πρόσβαλ εἰς εὐκρασίαν Οὕτω κατηθῶν εἶτ εἰς ἕτερον ἀγγεῖον Ψυχρὸν μάλασσε χερσὶ καὶ οὕτως τ’ ἀποτίθου Ἄλλην ὑπογράψω τῇ πρὸ ταύτης ὁμογενῆ Ποιεῖ δὲ πρὸς ἃ εἶπον ἔμπροσθεν πάθη Πάντων ἐπουλοῖ κρεῖττον αὕτη φαρμάκων Ἕλκη δυσαλθῆ καὶ τυλώδη καὶ χρόνια Τἀν τῷ προσώπῳ γινόμεν ἐξανθήματα Αὕτη θεραπεύει δίχα τινὸς δηγμοῦ κακοῦ Ἕδρας τ’ ἐχούσας ῥαγάδας καὶ σκληρίας Τὰς κονδυλώδεις καὶ τύλους ἀποβάλλεται Σκεύαζε δ’ οὕτως μνᾶν λιθαργύρου καλῆς Μνᾶ δέ ἐστι λίτρα καὶ τρίτον λίτρας μέρος Κηροῦ δὲ καλοῦ Ποντικοῦ μνᾶς ἥμισυ Ἰοῦ τέταρτον μνᾶς μέρος ξυστοῦ καλοῦ
translation_A: ...of all [ingredients] carefully; again let a little drip off; if you see it well-coloured and well-blended, lift the pot at once from the fire and add the resinous juice of all-heal, softened beforehand. But if the drug is harder by far, add oil to it for a good blending. Having strained it thus, then into another vessel; knead it cold with the hands, and so store it away. I shall set down another of the same kind as the one before it. It acts on the affections I mentioned before; this one cicatrizes better than all drugs ulcers hard to heal and callous and chronic; the eruptions that arise on the face this one cures without any bad biting; and seats that have fissures and hardnesses, the condylomatous ones, and it casts off calluses. Prepare it thus: a mina of good litharge - a mina is a litra and a third part of a litra; of good Pontic wax half a mina; of verdigris a fourth part of a mina, good scraped...
translation_B: of all the ingredients carefully; again let a little drip off; if you see it well-coloured and well-blended, take the pot at once from the fire and add galbanum, previously softened. But if the drug is by far too hard, add oil to it to a good blend. Having thus strained it, then into another vessel, cold, knead it with the hands and so store it away. I shall write below another, of the same kind as the one before it. It works against the affections I mentioned before; this one cicatrizes better than all drugs ulcers hard to heal, callous and chronic; the eruptions arising on the face this one cures without any harmful biting; and the fissures and hardnesses that the seat has, the condyloid ones, and calluses it casts off. Prepare it thus: a mina of good litharge, and a mina is a pound and a third part of a pound; of good Pontic wax half a mina; of good scraped verdigris a quarter part of a mina

greek: γε καὶ μετὰ ῥοδίνης κηρωτῆς ὀνίνησι μεγάλως πρὸς ἃ δὴ καὶ τὰς τοιαύτας διαθέσεις καὶ ἄλλα πολλὰ φάρμακα κατὰ τὸν ἑξῆς λόγον εἰρήσεται τινὰ μὲν ὁμοίαν ἔχοντα δύναμιν τῇ φοινικίνῃ τινὰ δὲ καὶ δραστικωτέραν πρὸς δὲ τὰ ῥευματικὰ πάντων ἄριστον φάρμακον τοῦτο καὶ πολλάκις ἐλπίδος τι μεῖζον ἀνύσαν ἐκπυήσαντος οὖν ποτε μηροῦ πλησίον τοῦ βουβῶνος ἀπέπτου τῆς καθ’ ὅλον αὐτὸν οὔσης φλεγμονῆς ἐσχηματίζετο μὲν ὑφ’ ἡμῶν τὸ σκέλος ὡς ἐκρεῖν τοὺς ἰχῶρας ἐπὶ τὸν βουβῶνα κατὰ δὲ τὸ γενόμενον ἕλκος ἐν πλέονι χρόνῳ τούτου συμβάντος ἐξεκενώθη μὲν τὸ κατασκῆψαν εἰς τὸν μηρὸν ῥεῦμα συριγγώδης δέ τις ἐγένετο διάθεσις ὑπὸ τῷ δέρματι καθ’ ὅλον τὸν μηρὸν ὡς βούλεσθαι μὲν διελεῖν αὐτὸν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐπιγονατίδος ὅπως ἑκατέρωθεν ἔκρους μὲν ὑπάρχῃ τοῖς ἰχῶρσιν
translation_A: indeed, also with rose cerate it helps greatly; against which indeed, and against such conditions, many other drugs too will be described in the discourse that follows, some having a power similar to the date plaster, some even more active. But against rheumatic conditions this is the best drug of all, and it has often accomplished something beyond hope. Once, then, when a thigh had suppurated near the groin, the inflammation over the whole of it being unconcocted, the leg was positioned by us so that the ichors would flow out toward the groin and through the ulcer that had formed; and this having come about over a longer time, the flux that had descended into the thigh was indeed evacuated, but a fistulous condition arose beneath the skin along the whole thigh, so that one wished to divide it near the patella, in order that there should be an outflow for the ichors on either side
translation_B: ...indeed, and with rose cerate it helps greatly against these; for which conditions, indeed, and for such conditions many other drugs will also be described in the following discourse, some having a power similar to the phoenicine, others even more active. But against conditions subject to a discharge or flux this is the best drug of all, and it has often accomplished something beyond hope. When once, then, a thigh had suppurated near the groin, the inflammation over the whole of it being unconcocted, the leg was positioned by us so that the ichors flowed out toward the groin and through the ulcer that had formed; and when this had gone on for a longer time, the flux that had settled into the thigh was evacuated, but a certain fistulous condition developed beneath the skin along the whole thigh, so that I wished to cut it open near the kneecap, in order that there might be an outflow for the ichors from both sides...

greek: δέ τι τῆς φλεγμονῆς αὐτοῦ σκιῤῥῶδες ὑπολείποιτο τῶν ἱκανῶς τι ξηραινόντων προσφέρειν ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἐφαίνετο λείπεσθαί τι τῷ διὰ τῆς ῥίζης τοῦ δρακοντίου φαρμάκῳ πρότερον ἐχρησάμην ὃ τὰ μὲν ἄλλα τὰ αὐτά ἔχει τῷ Αἰγυπτίῳ φαρμάκῳ τῇ ἴσιδι καλουμένῃ προσείληφε δὲ τὴν τοῦ δρακοντίου ῥίζαν ἐφεξῆς δὲ τούτου τῇ Ἀθηνᾷ καλουμένῃ χρησάμενος ἀπ ἐκείνης λοιπὸν ἐπὶ τὰ συνουλοῦντα παρεγενόμην ἐφ ἑτέρου δὲ τῷ διὰ τοῦ σιραίου λελυμένῳ τροχίσκῳ καταχρίων τὰ γεγυμνωμένα μέρη τοῦ τραύματος ἔξωθεν ἐπέβαλλον τὸ εὐφόρβιον ἀναμίξας κηρῷ καὶ ῥητίνῃ τοσούτοις τὸ πλῆθος ὡς ἐμπλαστρῶδές τε ἅμα γενέσθαι καὶ διασώζειν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ εὐφορβίου πῶς δ’ ἄν τις ἀποβλέπων πρὸς τούτους τοὺς σκοποὺς συνθείη τὸ φάρμακον ἐφεξῆς ἐρῶ καὶ γάρ τοι καὶ διὰ τοῦ ὄξους ἄλλο φάρμακον ἐποίησα
translation_A: ...but if something scirrhous of its inflammation should remain, to apply some of the agents that dry sufficiently. Since, then, something appeared to be lacking, I first used the drug made with the root of dracontium, which in all other respects has the same ingredients as the Egyptian drug called Isis, but has in addition the root of dracontium; and next after this, having used the one called Athena, I passed from that one to the cicatrizing agents for the remainder. In another case, smearing the bared parts of the wound with the troche made with boiled-down must, dissolved, I applied euphorbium on the outside, having mixed it with wax and resin of the pine in such quantity that it should both become plaster-like and at the same time preserve the power of the euphorbium. How one who looks to these aims should compound the drug I shall say next; for indeed I also made another drug with vinegar...
translation_B: but if something scirrhous of its inflammation should remain, to apply some of the things that dry sufficiently. Since, then, something appeared to be left over, I used first the drug made with the root of dracontium, which has the other ingredients the same as the Egyptian drug called Isis, but has taken in addition the root of dracontium; and next after this, having used the one called Athena, from that I went on thereafter to the cicatrizing agents. In another case, anointing the denuded parts of the wound with the troche dissolved in boiled-down must, I applied on the outside the euphorbium, having mixed it with wax and resin in such a quantity that it should at once become plaster-like and preserve the power of the euphorbium. How one, looking to these aims, should compound the drug I shall say next; for indeed I also made another drug with vinegar

greek: τὰ μεταλλικὰ σὺν ὄξει καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα προσεμβάλλων τὰ ξηρὰ καὶ πάλιν λειῶν εἶθ ὅταν ἔχῃ ταῦτα πηλώδη σύστασιν τὰ τηκτὰ μιγνὺς ὡς προείρηται ἄλλη ἀσφάλτου καὶ ῥητίνης τερμινθίνης καὶ πίσσης Βρυτίας ἀνὰ λίτραν α΄ ἐλαίου δραχ κδ΄ λιθαργύρου καὶ ψιμυθίου καὶ μάννης καὶ ἰοῦ καὶ λεπίδος καὶ ὀποπάνακος ἴσον ἑκάστου ταῖς εἴκοσι τέσσαρσι δραχμαῖς τοῦ ἐλαίου λαδάνου γο δύο ὅπερ ἐστὶ δραχ ιστ΄ καὶ δύο κοτύλας ὄξους ὁμοίως καὶ τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον τοῖς πρὸ αὐτοῦ δύο σκευάζεται ἄλλη χρυσοκόλλης καὶ λεπίδος καὶ στομώματος ἀνὰ δραχ δ΄ ἰοῦ δὲ καὶ χαλκάνθου ἑκατέρου τὸ ἥμισυ τουτέστιν ἀνὰ δραχ β΄ κηροῦ δραχ κε΄ τουτέστι γο γ΄ καὶ δραχμὴν μίαν ῥητίνης τερμινθίνης γο β΄ τουτέστιν δραχ ιστ΄ τὸν κηρὸν μετὰ τῆς τερμινθίνης τῆξον
translation_A: ...the metallic [ingredients] with vinegar, and after these adding the dry ones and triturating again; then, when these have a clay-like consistency, mixing in the meltable ones, as has been said before. Another: of bitumen and terebinth resin of the pine and Bruttian pitch, 1 litra each; of oil 24 drachmas; of litharge and white lead and manna and verdigris and scale and opopanax, each equal to the twenty-four drachmas of the oil; of ladanum two ounces, which is 16 drachmas; and two kotylai of vinegar. This drug too is prepared in the same way as the two before it. Another: of chrysocolla and scale and stomoma, 4 drachmas each; of verdigris and chalcanthum, half of each, that is 2 drachmas each; of wax 25 drachmas, that is 3 ounces and one drachma; of terebinth resin of the pine 2 ounces, that is 16 drachmas. Melt the wax with the terebinth...
translation_B: the metallic substances with vinegar, and after these adding the dry ingredients and levigating again; then, when these have a mud-like consistency, mixing in the meltable ingredients as has been said before. Another: of asphalt and of terebinth resin and of Bruttian pitch, one pound each; of oil, 24 drachms; of litharge and ceruse and manna and verdigris and scale and opopanax, of each an amount equal to the twenty-four drachms of the oil; of ladanum two ounces, which is 16 drachms; and two cotylae of vinegar. This drug too is prepared in the same way as the two before it. Another: of chrysocolla and scale and steel, 4 drachms each; of verdigris and of chalcanthum, half of each, that is 2 drachms each; of wax, 25 drachms, that is 3 ounces and one drachm; of terebinth resin, 2 ounces, that is 16 drachms. Melt the wax with the terebinth

greek: χοιράδας Στέλλουσα πᾶν οἴδημα καὶ τὰς ἥπατος Ἡ σπληνός γ ὑδαρεῖς διαθέσεις ἰωμένη Οὔρων ἄγουσα δαψιλεῖς τὰς ἐκκρίσεις Τὰς ἰσχιάδας λύει τε τὰς κεχρονισμένας Ταύτῃ Οὐλβιανὸς εὐφυὴς νεανίας Χρώμενος ὠφέλει πολλοὺς πάνυ Ἔχει δὲ λίτραν Ποντικοῦ κηροῦ μίαν Μίαν τε φρυκτῆς καἰ μίαν τῆς πιτυΐνης Ἀσβέστου τε προσφάτου οὐγγίαν α΄ Στυπτηρίας τε σχιστῆς οὐγγίαν α΄ Ἴσον δ’ ἑνὶ τούτων ἀῤῥενικοῦ τοῦ Ποντικοῦ Τούτοις παραχέας ὄξος εὐῶδες βραχὺ Λέαινε ἐφ ἱκανὸν ἐν θυείᾳ μείζονι Κηρῷ δὲ ῥητίνῃ τε προσβαλὼν βραχὺ Ἔλαιον τήξας ἐπὶ πυρὸς λάβρου φλογὸς Μιγνύς τ’ ἐπιμελῶς πάντα καὶ μαλάγματα Ποιῶν τ’ ἀμολύντου τὸ πάχος ἔχ ἀποκείμενον Χρώμενος ἐφ ὧν δεῖ προσφάτῳ τῷ σπληνίῳ Ἔλεγε δ’ ὁ Κράτιστος καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ φαρμάκου Καὶ πρὸς νόσων τε τῶν μακρῶν ἀπαλλαγὰς
translation_A: scrofulous swellings, reducing every oedema, and healing the watery conditions of liver or spleen, bringing on abundant excretions of urine, and it resolves chronic sciaticas. Using this, Ulpianus, a gifted young man, helped very many. It has one litra of Pontic wax, one of roasted [resin] and one of the pine [resin], of fresh quicklime one ounce, of split alum one ounce, equal to one of these of Pontic arsenic. Pouring on these a little fragrant vinegar, grind sufficiently in a larger mortar; adding to the wax and resin a little oil, having melted it over a fire of vigorous flame, and mixing all carefully and making soft masses, making it the thickness of a non-soiling one, keep it in store, using it where needed on a fresh compress. Kratistos, the father of the drug, also said that for the relief of long diseases
translation_B: scrofulous swellings; reducing every oedema, and healing the watery conditions of the liver or spleen; bringing on copious discharges of urine; and it resolves chronic sciaticas. Using this, Ulpianus, a gifted young man, benefited very many people. It contains one litra of Pontic wax, one of roasted [resin] and one of the pine [resin], of fresh quicklime 1 ounce, of split alum 1 ounce, and of Pontic orpiment an amount equal to one of these. Pouring a little fragrant vinegar over these, triturate sufficiently in a larger mortar; adding a little oil to the wax and the resin of the pine, melting it over a fire of fierce flame, mixing everything carefully, and making it into malagmata, bringing it to the thickness of a non-soiling drug, keep it in store. Use it, where needed, on a fresh compress. Kratistos, the father of the drug, said also that for the relief of long diseases

greek: καθάπερ τῇ ῥητίνῃ τε καὶ τῇ πίττῃ διὰ τοῦτο μιγνύω τῇ κηρωτῇ ῥητίνην ἢ πίτταν ἢ ἑκατέρου μέρος εὔδηλον οὖν ὅτι τούτων μιγνυμένων οὐκέτι τὸ ἔλαιον ἴσον αὐτοῖς ἐμβλητέον ὁ μὲν γὰρ κηρὸς εἰς ὑγρότητα πολλοῦ δεῖται τοῦ λίπους αἱ ῥητίναι δὲ αἱ μὲν ξηραὶ παντάπασιν ὀλίγου χρῄζουσιν αἱ δὲ ὑγραὶ καὶ προσλαβεῖν τινα ξηρὰν οὐσίαν ἐθέλουσιν εἰς ἐμπλαστρώδη σύστασιν ἐν μὲν οὖν τοῖς κηροῖς οὐ πολλή τίς ἐστιν ἡ διαφορὰ καθ’ ὑγρότητα καὶ ξηρότητα ταῖς ῥητίναις δ’ ἔμπαλιν ὥσπερ καὶ τῇ πίττῃ παμπόλλη ἡ διαφορὰ ταῖς ξηραῖς ἐστι πρὸς τὰς ὑγράς ξηροτάτη μὲν οὖν τῶν ῥητινῶν ἐστιν ἣν ὀνομάζουσί τινες φρυκτὴν τινὲς δὲ κολοφωνίαν δευτέρα δ’ ἡ ἐκ τῶν κεραμείων ἀκάθαρτός τε καὶ ἄφρυκτος ἐὰν δ’ αὐτὴν καθάρῃ τις
translation_A: as with resin and pitch. For this reason I mix with the cerate resin or pitch or a part of each. It is clear, then, that when these are mixed in, the oil is no longer to be put in equal to them; for wax needs much fat for moistness, but of the resins the entirely dry need little, while the moist even want to take in some dry substance for a plaster-like consistency. Among waxes, then, the difference in moistness and dryness is not great, but in resins, conversely, as also in pitch, the difference of the dry from the moist is very great. The driest of the resins, then, is the one some call roasted, others Colophonian; second is that from the potteries, unpurified and unroasted; but if one purifies it
translation_B: just as with the resin of the pine and the pitch. For this reason I mix into the cerate resin of the pine or pitch, or a portion of each. It is quite clear, then, that when these are mixed in, the oil is no longer to be put in equal to them; for wax needs much fat for moistness, while of the resins of the pine the wholly dry ones require little, and the moist ones even want to take in some dry substance in addition to reach a plaster-like consistency.
